takeaway: Isolated ST depression in V1 and V2 suggests posterior myocardial ischaemia, most likely from the posterior descending artery, supplied by the right coronary or the circumflex artery.

question.text: Postoperative chest pain; ECG shows tachycardia and isolated ST depression in V1 and V2. Which coronary artery is most likely responsible?

lines.text: The monitor shows a fast heart rate in a patient with chest pain.
ST depression across all leads would mean ischaemia, or angina.
But here the ST depression is isolated, in leads V1 and V2 only.
Those leads look at the heart from the front, so they see the posterior wall like a mirror.
lines.say: Those leads look at the heart from the front, so they see the posterior wall like a mirror. (laugh)

lines.text: ST depression there points to a posterior myocardial infarction.
The artery behind that is the posterior descending artery.
The right coronary or circumflex can supply it, and the ECG alone cannot tell which.
